question: What kind of mistake happens when a busy nurse accidentally documents care in someone else's chart?

options.A: Data omission
options.B: Transcription error
options.C: Duplicate entry
options.D: Wrong-patient charting

explanation: Entering notes into the wrong file is a risky mix-up that usually happens when things get too rushed on the ward. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T7#GNS113_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is a very common cause of death in babies suffering from neonatal tetanus?

options.A: Complete bone demineralization
options.B: Severe kidney failure and fluid overload
options.C: Asphyxia from respiratory muscle spasms
options.D: Massive internal gastrointestinal bleeding

explanation: Correct! Spasms in the throat and chest muscles can block the airway, quickly leading to a lack of oxygen (asphyxia) if not managed. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T018#GNS226_U3_T018_h7)

question: What is the main difference between a delayed union and a nonunion?

options.A: Delayed union requires surgery, while nonunion heals on its own with rest.
options.B: Delayed union takes longer than normal, while nonunion fails to heal entirely.
options.C: Delayed union involves infection, while nonunion is caused by blood clots.
options.D: Delayed union happens in children, while nonunion happens only in the elderly.

explanation: Think of delayed union as a slow student who eventually finishes the exam, while nonunion means the student simply gave up and stopped trying altogether. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T23#GNS222_U1_T23_h8)

question: Where do the majority of the lymphatic vessels of the breast drain?

options.A: Cervical lymph nodes
options.B: Axillary lymph nodes
options.C: Mediastinal nodes
options.D: Inguinal lymph nodes

explanation: About 75% of breast lymph fluid drains into the axillary lymph nodes located in the armpit area. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h6)

question: Which of these expenses is considered an indirect cost in a hospital?

options.A: Electricity used to light the entire hospital building
options.B: Bandages applied to a specific wound on a patient
options.C: The specific medication prescribed for hypertension
options.D: Surgical instruments sterilized for one specific operation

explanation: General electricity benefits everyone in the hospital, so you can't assign it to just one patient chart. That's why it's indirect! [learn more](GST322_U2_T2#GST322_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why do community health nurses need to adjust their standard routines during village outreach?

options.A: Government policies prohibit giving injections outside of clinics
options.B: Field conditions and local environments vary greatly compared to hospitals
options.C: Community members refuse standard hospital documentation forms
options.D: Vaccines given outdoors lose their chemical composition entirely

explanation: Outreach doesn't have the fancy setup of a hospital ward, so nurses get creative to keep things safe and sterile outside! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h1)

question: A newly qualified staff nurse guides a student on proper wound dressing technique. What does this situation demonstrate?

options.A: Formal ward management
options.B: Strict administrative control
options.C: Delegation of illegal tasks
options.D: Everyday nursing leadership

explanation: Guiding and teaching colleagues during clinical care is a form of leadership that any nurse can and should practice. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h1)

question: As a nurse, why would you start a patient on nasal oxygen therapy?

options.A: To treat tissue hypoxia and raise low blood oxygen levels
options.B: To deliver high-pressure aerosolized medications to the lungs
options.C: To completely replace normal breathing mechanics during sleep
options.D: To prevent the patient from experiencing dry mouth overnight

explanation: Spot on! We give oxygen when the body's tissues aren't getting enough of it (hypoxia), helping to bring those blood oxygen levels back up to a safe place. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T9#GNS212_U2_T9_h1)

question: A 16-year-old girl visits your clinic for family planning advice but is terrified her parents will find out. How should you respond as a nurse?

options.A: Scold her for engaging in premarital relationships
options.B: Refuse service and call her parents immediately
options.C: Assure her of confidentiality and provide age-appropriate counseling
options.D: Report her to local law enforcement authorities

explanation: Trust is everything in nursing! By assuring her of confidentiality, you make her feel safe enough to get the right health education and protection instead of hiding risky situations. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why don't we usually place supercomputers at a patient's bedside in a general ward?

options.A: They are too fragile to be touched by clinical nursing staff
options.B: They cannot process digital data formats used in nursing notes
options.C: Their immense processing power is unnecessary and impractical for daily clinical charting
options.D: They lack the ability to connect to modern electrical wall sockets

explanation: Exactly. Using a supercomputer for normal bedside charting is like using a cargo plane to drive to the local market—complete overkill! [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h6)

question: An asthma patient taking steroid medications suddenly has high blood sugar readings. What should you suspect?

options.A: Severe dehydration from lack of water intake
options.B: Medication-induced alteration of glucose metabolism
options.C: A primary failure of the pancreas to produce insulin
options.D: An allergic reaction to the asthma medication

explanation: Spot on! Steroid therapy frequently messes with normal blood sugar control, even in people who have never had diabetes before. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T2#GNS222_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which environmental hazard is most commonly removed to prevent falls in a home care setting?

options.A: Solid dining tables
options.B: Heavy wooden wardrobes
options.C: Loose scatter rugs
options.D: Ceiling light fixtures

explanation: Loose rugs easily slip underfoot or catch walking aids, making them a major hazard for elderly clients with poor balance. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T4#GNS324_U5_T4_h5)

question: Why do some drugs need a much higher dose when swallowed as pills compared to being given through an injection?

options.A: Intravenous drugs take longer to dissolve than liquid syrups or crushed pills.
options.B: First-pass metabolism in the liver inactivates a large portion of the oral dose.
options.C: Oral tablets contain inactive fillers that block the active ingredient completely.
options.D: The stomach acid destroys all intravenous drugs before they enter the arm veins.

explanation: When you swallow a pill, it goes straight to the liver via the gut first. The liver breaks a lot of it down before it even reaches the rest of the body! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T1#GNS125_U5_T1_h6)

question: When is a simple hand wash with ordinary soap and water best to use?

options.A: After handling visibly soiled items or using the restroom
options.B: Immediately before inserting a central venous catheter
options.C: Before assisting in major open-heart surgery
options.D: When hands are completely dry and free of visible dirt

explanation: When your hands are visibly dirty or messy, plain soap and water are your best friends for a physical clean-up. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a recommended way to reduce the spread of STIs in men?

options.A: Stopping all antibiotic use to boost natural immunity
options.B: Participating in routine periodic screening tests
options.C: Ensuring prompt treatment of all identified sexual partners
options.D: Consistent and correct use of latex barrier condoms

explanation: Stopping antibiotics is a huge no-no! It leads to treatment failure and superbugs, not immunity. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h8)

question: Which descriptive statistic represents the exact middle value of a dataset?

options.A: Mode
options.B: Median
options.C: Mean
options.D: Standard deviation

explanation: The median splits the dataset directly in half, with fifty percent of the values above it and fifty percent below. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T3#GNS224_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why must you teach patients never to stop their blood pressure medication suddenly?

options.A: It leads to sudden severe hair loss within hours.
options.B: It permanently damages the liver enzymes.
options.C: It can trigger dangerous rebound hypertension.
options.D: It will cause an immediate permanent loss of taste.

explanation: Spot on! Stopping blood pressure meds abruptly can cause blood pressure to shoot right back up to dangerous levels. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T2#GNS313_U3_T2_h5)

question: During which weeks of pregnancy is a baby most at risk for birth defects from harmful drugs?

options.A: The first two weeks following conception
options.B: The final two weeks before anticipated birth
options.C: Weeks three through eight of the first trimester
options.D: Throughout the entire third trimester

explanation: This is the major window when little organs are actively forming (organogenesis), making weeks 3 to 8 the most sensitive time. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T5#GNS215_U6_T5_h3)

question: A nurse wants to know the exact percentage of pregnant women at an antenatal clinic who sleep under treated mosquito nets. What type of question is this?

options.A: Descriptive
options.B: Causal
options.C: Relational
options.D: Interventional

explanation: You got this! Descriptive questions simply paint a picture of what is happening right now in a specific group of people. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T8#GNS217_U3_T8_h3)

question: Why is it important to teach digital health topics in nursing school?

options.A: To replace traditional bedside clinical practice with computer gaming
options.B: To prepare student nurses for modern virtual communication and digital care delivery
options.C: To ensure students never have to care for physical patients in wards
options.D: To teach students how to repair broken telephone network towers

explanation: Spot on! Healthcare is changing fast. Learning digital health early equips you with the skills you need for modern nursing practice. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T7#GNS113_U3_T7_h7)

question: What is one of the best ways patients can prevent malaria at home?

options.A: Avoiding all contact with domestic farm animals
options.B: Boiling all household cooking oil before use
options.C: Taking a daily dose of metronidazole as a vitamin
options.D: Sleeping under insecticide-treated bed nets every night

explanation: You've got this! Insecticide-treated nets create a protective shield against those nighttime Anopheles mosquito bites. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T5#GNS223_U3_T5_h8)

question: How does cutting back on coffee and energy drinks help a patient dealing with an anxiety disorder?

options.A: It prevents central nervous system stimulation that mimics anxiety symptoms
options.B: It guarantees uninterrupted sleep for twelve hours every night
options.C: It acts as a powerful direct replacement for antidepressant medication
options.D: It cures the genetic predisposition linked to panic disorder

explanation: Correct! Caffeine is a stimulant that causes jitteriness and a fast pulse—things you definitely don't need when managing anxiety. Smart choice! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T1#GNS324_U4_T1_h6)

question: Why are abstinence-only education programs often insufficient for protecting teenagers?

options.A: They force schools to close down health clinics
options.B: They cause physical delays in the maturation of the prefrontal cortex
options.C: They encourage teenagers to read explicit material online instead
options.D: They fail to give youth who become active the practical skills needed to prevent diseases and pregnancies

explanation: While abstinence is important, withholding practical information about contraception leaves sexually active teens completely unprotected. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h8)

question: How do post-disaster debriefing sessions help nursing teams improve over time?

options.A: They allow staff to share real-world experiences and update protocols based on actual findings
options.B: They ensure that all medical equipment is automatically cleaned without human effort
options.C: They replace the need for conducting regular mock disaster simulations
options.D: They guarantee that future disasters will never happen in the local community

explanation: Listening to frontline nurses talk about what actually happened on the ground gives us the best feedback to upgrade our emergency guidelines! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T7#GNS315_U1_T7_h10)

question: A nurse finds a 5-year-old child with sudden, floppy weakness in both legs. What is the best immediate nursing response?

options.A: Advise the family to stay indoors and avoid all local clinic visits
options.B: Report the case as an AFP emergency and collect stool samples
options.C: Prescribe broad-spectrum oral antibiotics for home management
options.D: Reassure the parents that normal muscle tone will return in a day

explanation: Wonderful clinical thinking! Any sudden floppy weakness in a child must be treated as an AFP emergency with urgent reporting and samples. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h6)

question: What does the term 'crossed signs' mean when talking about brain stem injuries?

options.A: Loss of vision in both eyes combined with hearing loss
options.B: Complete paralysis of both arms and both legs equally
options.C: Facial deficits on one side with body deficits on the other
options.D: Inability to breathe while maintaining normal heart rate

explanation: Crossed signs happen when cranial nerve damage affects the face on one side, while other pathway damages affect the body on the opposite side. It creates a crossed pattern of symptoms! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h6)

question: What is the best way to describe mental health in nursing?

options.A: Having an intelligence score far above the average
options.B: The total absence of any psychological distress or worry
options.C: A state of complete emotional and physical numbness
options.D: A state of well-being where a person can cope with normal stress

explanation: Mental health isn't just about never feeling sad or stressed. It's about having the coping skills to handle everyday pressures, work productively, and contribute to your community. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS314_U1_T1#GNS314_U1_T1_h1)

question: How do State Health Insurance Agencies usually differ from the federal NHIA initiative?

options.A: They only provide care for surgical emergencies in private clinics
options.B: They prohibit civil servants from accessing any form of medical care
options.C: They focus heavily on covering informal sector workers and rural dwellers in their states
options.D: They are funded exclusively by grants from foreign international banks

explanation: You're getting it! While federal schemes started with government workers, state agencies make special efforts to reach traders, artisans, and rural villagers. [learn more](GST322_U5_T4#GST322_U5_T4_h5)

question: What happens to a DRF if its extra cash is constantly pulled out to fund unrelated hospital projects?

options.A: The cost of purchasing medicines from wholesale vendors will drop
options.B: Patient satisfaction scores will rise due to improved hospital buildings
options.C: The pharmacy will automatically attract more international donors
options.D: The fund will eventually collapse and fail to restock essential drugs

explanation: Correct! If you drain the pharmacy's working capital for other things, you won't have enough cash left to replace sold medications when prices go up. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T2#GNS215_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary abnormal protein found in the red blood cells of a person with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Haemoglobin F
options.B: Haemoglobin C
options.C: Haemoglobin A
options.D: Haemoglobin S

explanation: The genetic mutation in sickle cell anaemia specifically leads to the production of abnormal haemoglobin S, which changes the shape of the red blood cells when it loses oxygen. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h1)

question: How does the ongoing brain drain impact the nurses who decide to stay and practice in Nigeria?

options.A: They automatically receive double salaries from government funds
options.B: They are barred from attending professional nursing conferences
options.C: They must close down all public primary health centers
options.D: They face heavier workloads, burnout, and dangerous nurse-to-patient ratios

explanation: That's right. When colleagues leave, the remaining nurses have to pick up the slack, leading to severe exhaustion and stretched resources. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h6)

question: What constitutes a 'shift' on a run chart according to standard interpretation rules?

options.C: Five or more consecutive points moving in one direction
options.D: Two data points crossing over the median line rapidly

explanation: A shift is defined as at least six consecutive points falling entirely above or entirely below the median line. [learn more](GST319_U1_T3#GST319_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which level of the Nigerian healthcare system includes federal teaching hospitals and specialized medical centers?

options.A: Community healthcare level
options.B: Secondary healthcare level
options.C: Tertiary healthcare level
options.D: Primary healthcare level

explanation: Teaching hospitals and federal medical centers operate at the tertiary level to provide advanced and specialized care. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h1)

question: How often should you check mum's vital signs and uterus during her very first hour after delivery?

options.A: Only once at the end of the shift
options.B: Every hour
options.C: Every 4 hours
options.D: Every 15 minutes

explanation: That first hour is high-alert time for postpartum hemorrhage. Frequent 15-minute checks let you catch any sneaky bleeding early. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h9)

question: A patient scheduled for a procedure with mild sedation asks for a glass of water an hour beforehand. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Explain that fasting guidelines must be followed to prevent aspiration during sedation.
options.B: Ignore the question because fluid intake does not affect anesthesia safety.
options.C: Tell the patient to drink plenty of fluids to stay hydrated before the test.
options.D: Allow the patient to drink a small cup of water since it is just a liquid.

explanation: Fasting (NPO) keeps the stomach empty so the patient doesn't accidentally choke or inhale stomach contents while sedated. Safety first! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T4#GNS321_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is a major limitation of relying solely on prevalence studies?

options.A: They are completely illegal to conduct in rural community settings
options.B: They can be affected by survival bias, missing those who died quickly
options.C: They cost more money than any other form of scientific research
options.D: They only measure future health risks and ignore current problems

explanation: Prevalence only counts current survivors, missing individuals who died rapidly before being surveyed. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h7)

question: What is the primary difference between an arranged marriage and a forced marriage?

options.A: The involvement of religious leaders
options.B: The age of the individuals getting married
options.C: The right to refuse and give full consent
options.D: The geographic location of the ceremony

explanation: In an arranged marriage, the individuals still have the freedom to say no, whereas a forced marriage happens without their consent. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h1)

question: Which collaborative platform is most commonly integrated directly into secure hospital software systems?

options.A: Public social networks
options.B: Standard text messaging
options.C: Personal email accounts
options.D: Microsoft Teams

explanation: Microsoft Teams is built to integrate smoothly with enterprise healthcare software for secure internal communication and file sharing. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h4)

question: What causes the nutritional paradox where a person is both overweight and undernourished?

options.A: Eating many cheap calories that lack essential micronutrients
options.B: Absorbing too many vitamins from cheap processed snacks
options.C: Consuming too much pure water alongside sugary drinks
options.D: Exercising too much while eating high-protein diets

explanation: When people fill up on cheap, heavy foods, they get plenty of energy (calories) but miss out on crucial vitamins and minerals. Great job thinking this through! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h2)

question: How do interferons protect your body from viral infections?

options.A: They wrap around viruses and digest them.
options.B: They raise body temperature to burn up viral particles.
options.C: They warn nearby healthy cells to put up their defenses against viruses.
options.D: They tell the bone marrow to make extra red blood cells.

explanation: Think of interferons as chemical text messages sent by infected cells to warn their healthy neighbors: 'A virus is coming, lock your doors!' [learn more](GST114_U4_T4#GST114_U4_T4_h6)

question: A community health nurse notices many young people in her village developing untreated high blood pressure. What action best reflects modern primary health care nursing practice?

options.A: Waiting inside the urban teaching hospital for patients to travel and find her
options.B: Focusing solely on childhood immunizations and ignoring adult health entirely
options.C: Organizing a local screening camp combined with lifestyle and diet counseling
options.D: Telling the villagers that chronic illnesses cannot be managed at the local level

explanation: Proactive community screening and health education bring prevention and early management directly to the people, fulfilling PHC goals. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h7)

question: A patient walks into the clinic with a mild ankle sprain and stable vital signs. What triage level fits best?

options.A: Urgent
options.B: Non-urgent
options.C: Resuscitation
options.D: Emergent

explanation: A stable injury that just needs a quick check or an X-ray falls right into our non-urgent category. Simple and straightforward! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h3)

question: How do humans usually catch hydatid disease?

options.A: Bites from infected mosquitoes
options.B: Inhalation of airborne cyst spores
options.C: Fecal-oral ingestion of parasite eggs
options.D: Direct skin penetration by larvae

explanation: It usually happens by accidentally swallowing microscopic eggs from dog feces via contaminated food, water, or unwashed hands. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T25#GNS313_U2_T25_h3)

question: When should physical or chemical restraints be used during a behavioral crisis?

options.A: Whenever the nursing staff feels mildly inconvenienced
options.B: As the very first step for any agitated patient
options.C: As a last resort when safety is at immediate risk
options.D: Only when ordered by a family member

explanation: Restraints are restrictive and carry risks, so they are only used when all verbal de-escalation fails and someone is in danger of being hurt. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T1#GNS315_U2_T1_h5)

question: In the rapid primary survey ABCDE framework, what does the letter 'C' stand for?

options.A: Contusion
options.B: Cognition
options.C: Circulation
options.D: Coma

explanation: You got it! 'C' stands for circulation, which means checking pulses, blood pressure, and stopping any heavy bleeding. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T3#GNS315_U1_T3_h4)

question: How does evidence-based nutrition mainly differ from traditional food folklore?

options.A: It changes every single day without any consistency
options.B: It relies on scientific testing, trials, and biochemical data
options.C: It completely ignores what local communities like to eat
options.D: It focuses only on expensive imported foods from abroad

explanation: Evidence-based nutrition uses systematic scientific research to prove what foods actually do inside the human body, keeping our care safe and reliable. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T017#GNS227_U2_T017_h5)

question: When is an individual digital message most appropriate in a clinical setting?

options.A: For posting general holiday notices on a public forum
options.B: For broadcasting emergency drills to the whole hospital
options.C: For publishing weekly hospital menus to the general public
options.D: For sharing quick, specific updates about a single patient

explanation: One-on-one digital messages are ideal for targeted, rapid communication regarding a specific patient's immediate needs. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why do we routinely test the mother's urine for protein and acetone during active labour?

options.A: It proves whether the mother has taken her prescribed iron tablets
options.B: It helps identify pre-eclampsia and maternal starvation or dehydration
options.C: It measures the exact blood sugar level of the unborn baby
options.D: It determines the precise gestational age in weeks

explanation: Urine checks are quick lifesavers! Protein can point towards pre-eclampsia, while acetone tells you if the mother is running out of energy or getting dehydrated. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h5)

question: When is the right time to start the secondary survey?

options.A: Only after the patient is discharged home
options.B: While the patient is actively in cardiac arrest
options.C: Before checking if the patient has a clear airway
options.D: After the primary survey is done and the patient is stable

explanation: Always make sure immediate life threats in the primary survey are handled before moving on to a detailed secondary survey. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T2#GNS315_U3_T2_h4)

question: How do pests like rats and flies make unmanaged hospital rubbish so dangerous?

options.A: They physically carry pathogens from the waste back into living and treatment areas
options.B: They consume all the toxic chemicals and render the waste completely harmless
options.C: They increase the rate at which biodegradable plastics break down in the sun
options.D: They serve as reliable biological indicators for routine environmental audits

explanation: Exactly! Pests feed on infectious waste and can transfer dangerous germs right back into patient care areas. Good job catching that! [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h1)

question: Why do we need special care when doing research with vulnerable groups?

options.A: To prevent exploitation and protect them from harm
options.B: Because they always pay large amounts of money
options.C: To satisfy international tourism guidelines
options.D: So the researcher can finish data collection quickly

explanation: Vulnerable patients need extra protection because they might easily feel pressured to agree to a study. Keeping them safe is our top priority. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is the best way to tell if a food safety training program actually worked?

options.A: Watching to see if workers practice safe habits on the kitchen floor
options.B: Making sure everyone memorized the manual word-for-word
options.C: Calculating how much money was spent on the workshop
options.D: Checking that everyone sat through every minute of the lecture

explanation: Real learning shows in daily habits! True success is when staff actually use what they learned while cooking and cleaning. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h8)

question: What is the main job of freshwater snails in the life cycle of schistosomes?

options.A: They transport the parasite permanently out of aquatic environments.
options.B: They consume human waste to reduce overall environmental egg counts.
options.C: They serve as the definitive host where adult worms reproduce sexually.
options.D: They act as intermediate hosts where asexual multiplication occurs.

question: Which retinal photoreceptor cells are primarily responsible for seeing fine details and colors in bright daylight?

options.A: Rod cells
options.B: Cone cells
options.C: Corneal cells
options.D: Scleral cells

explanation: Cones thrive in bright light and provide high-acuity color vision, unlike rods which function best in dim light. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h4)

question: What is a major operational challenge when using MBO in a hospital?

options.A: Nurses refusing to care for patients under any circumstance
options.B: Patients demanding to set their own medical treatment goals
options.C: A complete lack of computers in all medical wards
options.D: Constant unpredictability and emergencies disrupting plans

explanation: Healthcare environments are volatile, making rigid adherence to long-term goals difficult during crises. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h6)

question: How do waterborne diseases like cholera and typhoid usually spread?

options.B: Direct skin contact with industrial chemical waste
options.C: Mosquito bites near stagnant ponds and rivers
options.D: Ingestion of water contaminated with fecal matter

question: Why do nurses need to work closely with logistics officers during an emergency?

options.A: To negotiate international trade agreements for pharmaceutical manufacturing
options.B: To ensure fragile medical supplies like vaccines remain viable during transport

options.D: To manage the financial bank accounts of the Ministry of Health
