question: What is a major benefit of a midwife engaging with traditional leaders and birth attendants?

options.A: Training them to perform major cesarean sections independently
options.B: Encouraging early antenatal booking and formal facility delivery
options.C: Taking over the administration of local government offices
options.D: Eliminating the need for any primary health care clinics

explanation: Partnering with community figures helps build trust and directs pregnant women toward skilled birth attendance at health facilities. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h5)

question: Why is it important to evaluate the primary caregiver during a home visit?

options.A: Caregivers are legally responsible for paying the nurse's salary
options.B: Caregivers often experience burnout and physical exhaustion
options.C: Caregivers usually have the same psychiatric diagnosis
options.D: Caregivers make all clinical decisions without medical advice

explanation: Family caregivers carry immense stress supporting a mentally ill relative, making their well-being a crucial focus of home care. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h4)

question: During a menstrual check-up, which patient symptom is an immediate red flag that needs prompt clinical attention?

options.A: Soaking through a sanitary pad every hour for several hours in a row
options.B: Mild abdominal cramping on the first day of the period
options.C: A cycle length that varies by two days each month
options.D: Mild breast tenderness a week before menstruation begins

explanation: Soaking a pad every single hour for hours on end is never normal—it's a serious sign of heavy bleeding and potential hemorrhage that needs immediate help. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T4#GNS121_U5_T4_h7)

question: Which type of immunity is present from birth and reacts the same way to all foreign invaders?

options.A: Adaptive immunity
options.B: Artificial active immunity
options.C: Innate immunity
options.D: Natural passive immunity

explanation: Innate immunity is our built-in, non-specific defense system that responds immediately to any foreign threat without prior exposure. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which statement best describes informed consent in a longitudinal study?

options.A: It is an ongoing process that may need to be renewed as the study progresses
options.B: It is completely optional if the participants are hospital nurses
options.C: It is a one-time signature that never needs to be discussed again
options.D: It is only required on the very last day of data collection

explanation: Spot on! Because long studies evolve over time, participants should always remain informed and freely willing to continue. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T11#GNS224_U1_T11_h6)

question: A nurse checks a patient's pedal pulses and finds the left pulse is strong while the right pulse cannot be felt at all. What is the most immediate clinical concern?

options.A: High blood pressure throughout the body
options.B: A potential blockage in the right leg artery
options.C: An allergic reaction to heart medication
options.D: A normal variation in elderly patients

explanation: An absent pulse on only one side strongly suggests local arterial occlusion or injury, requiring urgent follow-up. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the main goal of doing a health assessment right inside a patient's home?

options.A: To enforce strict hospital rules in a private residential property
options.B: To evaluate how well a person manages their health in their daily living space
options.C: To replace the need for routine visits to the primary doctor
options.D: To test family members on basic nursing and medical procedures

explanation: Spot on! Home assessments help us see how patients truly cope with their health right where they live every day. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h1)

question: A patient has an abnormally low BMI. What major physiological complication are they most at risk for?

options.A: Increased bone mineral density and joint stiffness
options.B: Chronic elevation of systemic blood pressure
options.C: Impaired immune function and delayed wound healing
options.D: Excessive thickening of arterial walls from plaque buildup

explanation: Well done! Being severely underweight starves the body of essential nutrients, weakening immunity and slowing down how wounds heal. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T10#GNS121_U1_T10_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal way that toxic substances cause a medical emergency?

options.A: Disrupting cellular oxygen use at the tissue level
options.B: Blocking the normal electrical signals of the heart
options.C: Stimulating the production of healthy bone marrow cells
options.D: Causing sudden and profound systemic vasodilation

explanation: Making healthy blood cells in the bone marrow is a good, normal process! Toxins cause harm by damaging systems, not by boosting healthy growth. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h5)

question: How is rehabilitation nursing different from acute care nursing?

options.A: Curing sudden infections and trauma
options.B: Preventing initial exposure to contagious diseases
options.C: Managing terminal pain and palliative comfort
options.D: Restoring function and promoting adaptation

explanation: Acute care is all about saving lives and treating sudden illness, while rehab focuses on helping patients adapt and get back their independence. You've got this! [learn more](GNS123_U6_T1#GNS123_U6_T1_h1)

question: In a SMART aim, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

options.A: Mandatory
options.B: Measurable
options.C: Manual
options.D: Maximum

explanation: In the SMART goal framework, 'M' stands for measurable. It means your goal must include clear numbers or signs so you know if you are actually making progress. [learn more](GST319_U3_T3#GST319_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is a 'double-barreled' question in a research survey?

options.A: A question placed at the very end of a long research tool
options.B: A single question that mistakenly asks about two different things
options.C: A question that offers more than five possible answer choices
options.D: A survey item written in two different languages at once

explanation: Double-barreled questions confuse respondents because they cannot give separate answers to two different ideas packed into one sentence. You'll master questionnaire design in no time! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h3)

question: Why is it important to note unexpected problems during the Do phase?

options.A: To make the paperwork as complicated as possible for staff
options.B: To prove to management that no changes were actually made
options.C: To ensure that nurses can be disciplined for making mistakes
options.D: To capture real-world challenges that will affect the study phase

explanation: Right! Knowing what went wrong in the busy clinical setting helps us understand our results much better later on. [learn more](GST319_U3_T5#GST319_U3_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following actions is NOT appropriate when a nurse discovers a severely irregular pulse in a resting patient?

options.A: Notify the attending physician promptly about the irregular rhythm
options.B: Wait until the end of the shift to report the finding
options.C: Review the medication record for heart-altering drugs
options.D: Assess the patient for dizziness, chest pain, or shortness of breath

explanation: Waiting to report an acute abnormal finding puts the patient at risk; abnormal signs require prompt assessment and notification. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h6)

question: Which of these is a well-known risk factor for developing preeclampsia?

options.A: Eating a high-protein diet
options.B: Carrying a fourth or fifth child
options.C: Being younger than 20 years old
options.D: First-time pregnancy (nulliparity)

explanation: First-time mums' bodies are experiencing pregnancy for the very first time, which statistically gives them a higher chance of developing preeclampsia. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T019#GNS226_U2_T019_h3)

question: Which of the following is a primary example of consumer health informatics?

options.A: University nursing curriculum accreditation databases
options.B: Internal staff attendance registers used by nurse managers
options.C: Patient portals and wearable fitness tracking applications
options.D: Hospital financial ledger and budgeting software programs

explanation: Consumer health informatics centers on tools that patients use directly to track and manage their personal health. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h6)

question: Apart from direct bedside nursing, what is another key role nurses play in tackling health barriers?

options.A: Passing national laws to regulate international drug importation
options.B: Advocating for health policy reforms and community education
options.C: Setting macroeconomic exchange rates for medical supplies
options.D: Financing the construction of federal tertiary hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Nurses use their frontline experiences to teach communities and push for system changes that make care more accessible. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h7)

question: A patient catches a hookworm infection after walking barefoot on damp, contaminated soil. How did the parasite get in?

options.A: Inhalation of airborne cysts
options.B: An infected insect bite
options.C: Direct skin penetration
options.D: Feco-oral contamination

explanation: Spot on! Some worm larvae are crafty enough to burrow right through the soft skin of bare feet. Always wear your shoes! [learn more](GST114_U6_T2#GST114_U6_T2_h4)

question: Why is follow-up after a referral so important for a community health nurse?

options.A: To collect payment for the transport fare used by the client
options.B: To confirm whether the client reached the facility and received the needed service
options.C: To audit the financial records of the tertiary hospital
options.D: To reverse the contraceptive method chosen by the client

explanation: Following up lets you close the loop! You get to check if your client actually made it safely and got the care they needed. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h4)

question: A community health team wants to know if their new malaria prevention posters were successful. What is the best way to check?

options.A: Ask the local printer if they enjoyed making the colorful graphic designs
options.B: Count how many posters are left neatly stacked inside the nurse's office drawer
options.C: Measure changes in community health habits, such as increased use of insecticide-treated nets
options.D: Assume success because the hospital director liked the color scheme

explanation: The real test of good communication is seeing actual behavior change and healthier habits in the community! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T4#GNS124_U5_T4_h6)

question: What does Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) allow nurses to do?

options.A: Print physical medication prescriptions automatically at home
options.B: Perform major surgical procedures over a live video stream
options.C: Replace all in-person nursing staff with computer software
options.D: Receive daily health readings sent from a patient's home device

explanation: RPM tools transmit vital signs and health metrics directly from the patient's home to healthcare providers for ongoing tracking. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h4)

question: A mother is scared that immunization injections will make her baby sick. How should you respond?

options.A: Scold her for ignoring professional medical advice
options.B: Explain normal mild side effects and reassure her about the benefits
options.C: Advise her to skip the injections entirely if she feels worried
options.D: Tell her that children never experience any discomfort from vaccines

explanation: Moms often worry! Taking a moment to calmly explain normal side effects like low fever builds great trust and helps keep babies on schedule. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T64#GNS214_U1_T64_h4)

question: Why don't we use traditional validity and reliability tests in qualitative research?

options.A: Computers cannot calculate statistics on words the same way they do numbers
options.B: Qualitative researchers do not care if their findings are accurate or true
options.C: Human experiences are subjective and cannot be measured with rigid consistency
options.D: Ethics boards forbid researchers from testing qualitative data for errors

explanation: Human feelings and experiences change and cannot be put into a rigid numerical box, so qualitative research uses different checks for quality. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T6#GNS224_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is the main focus of Behavioral Change Communication (BCC) in nutrition?

options.A: Addressing cultural habits and beliefs influencing food choices
options.B: Importing expensive nutritional supplements from abroad
options.C: Enforcing strict legal penalties for poor dietary habits
options.D: Conducting laboratory tests on food chemical safety

explanation: That's right! BCC looks past simple facts to understand the cultural and social reasons behind how people choose and prepare their meals. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h5)

question: At 32 weeks, a pregnant patient suddenly has high blood pressure and protein in her urine. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Pre-existing chronic glomerulonephritis
options.B: Pregnancy-induced renal complication
options.C: Asymptomatic bacteriuria progression
options.D: Congenital solitary kidney anomaly

explanation: Spotting new-onset blood pressure issues and protein after 20 weeks is a major classic sign of preeclampsia affecting the kidneys. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T007#GNS226_U4_T007_h2)

question: Which part of the brain acts as the body's natural thermostat during a fever?

options.A: Cerebellum
options.B: Hypothalamus
options.C: Thalamus
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: The hypothalamus is like the internal thermostat in your brain. It turns up the heat when your body needs to fight off an infection. [learn more](GST114_U4_T4#GST114_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which of these best describes permanent harm?

options.A: A temporary drop in blood pressure after changing positions
options.B: A lasting disability or loss of function caused by an error
options.C: A mild headache that resolves after sleeping overnight
options.D: An allergic rash that disappears after taking an antihistamine

explanation: Permanent harm means the patient suffers a long-term or irreversible loss of ability. This is why our daily safety checks are so important. [learn more](GST319_U5_T5#GST319_U5_T5_h3)

question: How does teaching communities about health help cut down on self-medication?

options.A: It lowers the market prices of imported pharmaceutical tablets
options.B: It gives every citizen a license to prescribe drugs to their neighbors
options.C: It helps people recognize when symptoms require a professional medical evaluation
options.D: It eliminates the need for hospitals by teaching home surgical techniques

explanation: When people know better, they seek professional help early instead of guessing solutions at home with dangerous drugs. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T1#GNS215_U4_T1_h7)

question: Why is keeping a narrow range for vital signs important for a patient?

options.A: It ensures the patient stays awake during the night
options.B: It guarantees that blood pressure never changes
options.C: It prevents vital organs from failing due to extreme stress
options.D: It stops the patient from needing any medication

explanation: Great thinking! Staying within a safe, normal range protects your patient's cells and organs from being overworked by extreme highs and lows. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T7#GNS123_U1_T7_h1)

question: The neural tube, which forms the brain and spinal cord, develops from which germ layer?

options.A: Endoderm
options.B: Trophoblast
options.C: Mesoderm
options.D: Ectoderm

explanation: Since the nervous system links closely with the skin and outer structures, it comes right from the ectoderm layer. Excellent recall! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h7)

question: A nurse is about to start an intravenous line for a patient with no known infections. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Put on a heavy rubber apron and shoe covers
options.B: Move the patient to an airborne isolation room
options.C: Ask the patient to wear a surgical mask
options.D: Perform hand hygiene and put on gloves

explanation: Standard precautions require hand hygiene and gloves before any procedure involving potential contact with blood or body fluids. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h3)

question: Why do researchers clean their data before running statistics?

options.A: To reduce the number of participants needed for the study
options.B: To catch entry mistakes and prevent false research results
options.C: To get extra funding from the hospital research committee
options.D: To make the research report shorter and easier to print

explanation: Data cleaning is like double-checking your medication dosage math—it catches errors early so your final results are accurate and safe. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T16#GNS217_U3_T16_h3)

question: A nurse uses a bedside barcode scanner before giving a drug. Which type of informatics does this represent?

options.A: Nursing research informatics
options.B: Consumer health informatics
options.C: Clinical nursing informatics
options.D: Nursing education informatics

explanation: Bedside verification tools directly support clinical workflows and patient safety, placing them squarely in clinical nursing informatics. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h2)

question: A nurse leaves the ward during a busy shift to run personal errands miles away and causes an accident. Who carries the blame?

options.A: The state nursing council
options.B: The hospital administration
options.C: The chief medical director
options.D: The nurse personally

explanation: Because the nurse was way out of bounds doing personal things away from work, the hospital escapes vicarious liability, leaving the nurse to face it alone. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of nursing orientation when starting at a new hospital?

options.A: To discipline nurses who break minor hospital uniform rules
options.B: To determine the annual leave days for all hospital staff
options.C: To introduce the employee to policies, layout, and team culture
options.D: To test the clinical speed of experienced foreign nurses

explanation: Orientation helps you find your way around, meet your new colleagues, and learn how things are done in that specific hospital so you feel right at home. [learn more](GST321_U4_T1#GST321_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why is noting a patient's biological sex important when taking an endocrine history?

options.A: It helps identify conditions like thyroid disorders that affect women more often
options.B: It dictates the exact calorie count the patient needs daily
options.C: It replaces the need to perform a complete review of systems
options.D: It proves whether the patient has a genetic metabolic disease

explanation: Well done! Knowing biological sex helps us suspect certain gender-linked conditions, like thyroid imbalances, right from the start. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T2#GNS222_U2_T2_h2)

question: Why shouldn't a nurse rely *only* on the p-value when deciding to change how patients are cared for?

options.A: Hospital administrators only look at qualitative nurse interviews
options.B: Journal articles often hide the actual t-statistic value
options.C: P-values cannot be trusted when sample sizes are large
options.D: Statistical significance does not guarantee meaningful clinical impact

explanation: Just because a finding is statistically 'real' doesn't mean it makes a big enough difference to change everyday bedside nursing practice. Always look at the clinical picture! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T14#GNS217_U4_T14_h7)

question: What role do normal bacterial flora play in the healthy vagina?

options.A: They assist with the physical transport of sperm cells
options.B: They supply blood directly to the uterine lining
options.C: They maintain an acidic environment to protect against pathogens
options.D: They produce hormones to regulate the menstrual cycle

explanation: Good bacteria like Lactobacillus produce acid, which stops harmful bacteria and fungi from multiplying. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h2)

question: What is the biggest risk if you start a research project with a topic that is too vague or broad?

options.A: The hospital administration will immediately ban the study
options.B: The study becomes too messy and hard to manage
options.C: Patients will refuse to take their medications
options.D: It guarantees the results will be published internationally

explanation: If your topic is too wide, you'll end up with mountains of random data that don't make sense. Narrowing it down keeps your project neat and stress-free. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T2#GNS217_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why is checking the damage so important after a disaster occurs?

options.A: It allows the government to fine citizens who failed to evacuate
options.B: It replaces the need for search and rescue operations
options.C: It guarantees that no future disasters will ever occur in that zone
options.D: It helps agencies quantify losses and plan effective recovery efforts

explanation: Damage assessments give a clear picture of what was destroyed, helping authorities know how to send help and rebuild properly. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h4)

question: A patient has vaginal bleeding, mild lower tummy cramps, but her cervix is still tightly closed. What kind of abortion is this?

options.A: Incomplete abortion
options.B: Threatened abortion
options.C: Inevitable abortion
options.D: Complete abortion

explanation: When bleeding and cramps happen but the cervix stays closed, it's called a threatened abortion because the pregnancy might still continue safely. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h1)

question: If a home care family is struggling financially and needs help finding community resources, who is the best professional to call?

options.A: Registered Dietitian
options.B: Wound Care Specialist
options.C: Medical Social Worker
options.D: Physical Therapist

explanation: Medical social workers are pros at navigating financial aid, government packages, and community support programs to help struggling families. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T2#GNS324_U2_T2_h8)

question: A patient trapped under a heavy collapsed wall beam is experiencing which type of asphyxiation?

options.A: Environmental oxygen displacement
options.B: Upper airway foreign body blockage
options.C: Mechanical restriction of the chest
options.D: Cellular poisoning from toxins

explanation: When heavy debris presses on the chest, it physically stops the ribcage from expanding. That's a classic mechanical restriction! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T8#GNS123_U3_T8_h3)

question: A hospital wants to choose between two identical blood pressure drugs that work equally well and are equally safe. Which analysis should they use?

options.A: Cost-Benefit Analysis
options.B: Cost-Minimization Analysis
options.C: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis
options.D: Cost-Utility Analysis

explanation: Since the clinical effects are identical, you only need to compare their price tags. Cost-minimization helps you pick the least costly option. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h3)

question: Long-term hookworm infection most commonly leads to which major health problem?

options.A: Chronic kidney failure
options.B: Elevated blood pressure
options.C: Obstructive jaundice
options.D: Iron-deficiency anemia

explanation: Hookworms hook onto the intestinal wall and feed on blood, which over time causes significant blood loss and leads to iron-deficiency anemia. [learn more](GST114_U3_T6#GST114_U3_T6_h4)

question: What does it mean when a patient's emotional distress is described as 'somaticized'?

options.A: Seeking immediate help from a specialized psychiatrist
options.B: Denying that any mental or physical health problem exists
options.C: Isolating oneself from family and friends during a crisis
options.D: Expressing emotional pain entirely through physical bodily complaints

explanation: Think of somaticization as the body speaking what the heart cannot. It's when emotional pain turns into very real physical signs like headaches, stomach aches, or crushing fatigue. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the main sign of a food fad?

options.A: It is a lifelong medical diet prescribed by a qualified physician.
options.B: It is a government-regulated nutrition program for school children.
options.C: It is a traditional cultural meal plan passed down for generations.
options.D: It is an intense and short-lived dietary trend without scientific backing.

explanation: Food fads come and go very quickly. They usually make big health claims that have zero real science behind them. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h1)

question: Why must you use the same data collection tools throughout a longitudinal study?

options.A: To make sure the research assistants do not have to work very hard
options.B: To ensure that measured changes are real and not caused by changing the measurement tool
options.C: To comply with rules about destroying old medical records
options.D: To keep the total budget of the research project at zero

explanation: Exactly! If you change your measuring instrument, you won't know if patient scores changed because their health changed or simply because the tool was different. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T11#GNS224_U1_T11_h5)

question: A nurse checks daily blood glucose numbers sent automatically from a patient's smart glucometer at home. What is this called?

options.A: Electronic health record archiving
options.B: Store-and-forward imaging
options.C: Remote patient monitoring
options.D: Synchronous tele-surgery

explanation: Great job! Remote patient monitoring uses connected home devices to keep an eye on vital signs without the patient needing to visit the clinic. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h2)

question: A patient with sickle cell disease suddenly has severe belly pain, a rapidly swelling spleen, and signs of shock. What dangerous complication is likely happening?

options.A: Cerebrovascular accident
options.B: Splenic sequestration
options.C: Bone marrow failure
options.D: Acute chest syndrome

explanation: This is called splenic sequestration. It happens when sickled cells get trapped inside the spleen, causing it to swell up fast and trapping a huge amount of the body's blood volume. It's a true emergency! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T14#GNS311_U2_T14_h2)

question: What is the primary goal of research dissemination?

options.A: Securing permanent funding from international organizations
options.B: Increasing the personal salary of the principal investigator
options.C: Filing completed documents in secure university archives
options.D: Sharing study results with people who can use them

explanation: Dissemination focuses on getting findings into the hands of those who can put them into practice to improve care or policy. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h1)

question: How can you tell the difference between morning joint stiffness in osteoarthritis versus inflammatory arthritis?

options.A: Osteoarthritis stiffness only affects the upper body joints.
options.B: Osteoarthritis stiffness never happens in the morning hours.
options.C: Osteoarthritis stiffness usually lasts less than thirty minutes.
options.D: Osteoarthritis stiffness gets worse the more the person moves.

explanation: Joint stiffness from wear-and-tear arthritis is brief after waking up, whereas inflammatory arthritis causes stiffness lasting an hour or more. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h3)

question: Why do healthcare teams use structured improvement steps instead of just trying random ideas?

options.A: Random solutions take longer to write on paper
options.B: Structured frameworks are legally required for every shift change
options.C: Hospital management bans staff from making quick decisions
options.D: Random solutions rarely solve the root cause of the clinical problem

explanation: Spot on! When we use a structured approach, we dig deep to find the real cause of an issue rather than just guessing and hoping for the best. [learn more](GST319_U3_T1#GST319_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the main goal of day and night hospital services?

options.A: To provide permanent housing for chronic psychiatric patients
options.B: To replace outpatient clinics entirely in rural areas
options.C: To isolate violent patients from their families permanently
options.D: To bridge the gap between full hospital admission and community life

explanation: Spot on! These services provide structured support while keeping patients connected to their families and everyday lives. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h1)

question: A 13-year-old girl comes to the clinic showing frequent injuries and signs of poor nutrition. What should be an early suspicion for the nurse?

options.A: Potential abuse and vulnerability linked to an early forced union
options.B: Normal developmental changes associated with puberty
options.C: A rare genetic metabolic disorder affecting bone strength
options.D: Intentional self-harm due to school academic pressure

explanation: Repeated injuries and malnutrition in a very young girl often point to domestic mistreatment and early marriage. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T9#GNS312_U1_T9_h6)

question: What is the main reason we monitor a child's growth at the clinic?

options.A: To detect growth problems before visible signs appear
options.B: To treat children who already have severe infections
options.C: To vaccinate children against common childhood illnesses
options.D: To provide free food supplies to low-income families

explanation: Spotting small changes in weight or height early lets you step in and help before severe malnutrition sets in. You've got this! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h1)

question: How often should you check the patient's breathing during the early phase of steam therapy?

options.A: Every four hours
options.B: Only when the patient rings the bell
options.C: Every fifteen minutes
options.D: Once every shift

explanation: Checking frequently at the start ensures the patient is taking in the moisture well and their breathing is improving. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T8#GNS212_U2_T8_h5)

question: Generally speaking, what happens to a computer's power as its physical size gets bigger?

options.A: It remains exactly the same as smaller units
options.B: It increases alongside storage capacity
options.C: It drops to zero without external monitors
options.D: It decreases significantly to save power

explanation: Exactly! Bigger physical size usually means more room for heavy-duty parts that can handle massive workloads and store tons of information. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which type of drug molecule is most likely to leave the body through the biliary system (bile) rather than the kidneys?

options.A: Tiny, water-soluble molecules
options.B: Large, fat-soluble compounds
options.C: Strongly ionized electrolytes
options.D: Volatile inhaled gases

explanation: Remember: small water-soluble molecules love going out through the kidneys, while the biliary system prefers larger, fat-soluble compounds! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T4#GNS125_U5_T4_h4)

question: Why are IPC rules still enforced in a quarantine zone where people feel healthy?

options.A: To test the durability of hospital cleaning supplies
options.B: Because residents might already be shedding germs before showing symptoms
options.C: To punish people for breaking travel rules
options.D: To replace the need for medical check-ups

explanation: Many infectious diseases can be transmitted by people who appear well but are in the late stages of incubation. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h5)

question: On an ECG machine, what does the QRS complex show us?

options.A: The heart resting and recovering
options.B: Upper chambers squeezing
options.C: Lower chambers relaxing
options.D: Lower chambers electrical activity before they squeeze

explanation: The big tall spike on the ECG screen (the QRS) is the electrical wave racing through the ventricles right before they pump blood out. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h5)

question: How does following hospital policies correctly affect patient outcomes?

options.A: It stops patients from needing any medications during admission
options.B: It guarantees that patients will never complain about food
options.C: It completely eliminates all diseases from the hospital ward
options.D: It reduces medical errors through consistent and safe practices

explanation: When everyone follows consistent safety checks, treatments are done right every time, which drastically lowers the risk of patient harm. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h6)

question: Which professional is best suited to help community nurses promote backyard farming?

options.A: Hospital biomedical engineer
options.B: Surgical theater technician
options.C: Emergency room pharmacist
options.D: Agricultural extension worker

explanation: Agricultural workers have the expertise in crop growing and farming techniques needed to support backyard gardens. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h7)

question: Why do patients with chronic hookworm infections often develop anemia?

options.A: Suppression of bone marrow by parasite toxins
options.B: Rapid destruction of red blood cells by the liver
options.C: A complete lack of dietary protein intake
options.D: Ongoing blood loss from intestinal attachment

explanation: Hookworms latch onto the inside of the intestines and feed on the host's blood. Over time, this steady loss adds up and leads to anemia. Makes total sense when you picture it! [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h4)

question: What happens during the acrosome reaction when a sperm reaches the outer layers of an egg?

options.A: Enzymes are released from the sperm head to digest a path through protective layers
options.B: The sperm tail falls off completely to anchor the head inside the follicle
options.C: The egg swallows the entire sperm tail without using any chemical help
options.D: Protective antibodies coat the sperm to prevent premature entry

explanation: Think of the acrosome as a tiny chemical drill at the tip of the sperm head, releasing special enzymes to clear a pathway through the egg's defenses. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h3)

question: Which test gives the definitive, 100% confirmation of CJD?

options.A: Chest X-ray examination
options.B: Complete blood cell count
options.C: Neuropathological brain tissue exam
options.D: Cerebrospinal fluid culture

explanation: You got it! While other tests help doctors look at clues, final confirmation requires checking brain tissue for those hallmark sponge-like changes. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which special structure helps single-unit smooth muscle cells contract together as one coordinated sheet?

options.A: Neuromuscular spindles
options.B: Desmosomes
options.C: Dense bodies
options.D: Gap junctions

explanation: Gap junctions act like open doorways between neighboring cells, letting electrical messages zip right through so they all squeeze together in harmony. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h4)

question: What is the best approach when advising a pregnant mum on a tight budget about her diet?

options.A: Insisting that she must purchase organic foods to have a healthy baby
options.B: Suggesting affordable, locally available food alternatives that meet her nutritional needs
options.C: Skipping dietary counseling because poverty makes nutrition impossible to change
options.D: Telling her to buy expensive imported supplements from specialized pharmacies

explanation: Great nursing care is practical and real! Always guide patients toward nourishing, budget-friendly local foods they can actually access. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h7)

question: How would you describe a keloid?

options.A: Overgrowth of thick scar tissue beyond the wound
options.B: A pale patch of skin lacking normal pigment
options.C: A temporary bruise caused by blunt trauma
options.D: An open skin ulcer that refuses to heal

explanation: Correct! Keloids happen when the skin produces extra collagen during healing, creating firm, raised scars that spread past the original cut. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T7#GNS225_U6_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a urinary catheter?

options.A: To deliver fluids directly into the kidneys
options.B: To prevent the formation of kidney stones
options.C: To drain urine from the bladder
options.D: To measure the capacity of the ureters

explanation: A catheter is a flexible tube inserted through the urethra specifically to allow urine to drain out of the bladder when a patient cannot do so naturally. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T20#GNS212_U1_T20_h1)

question: What does decentralized decision-making mean in primary nursing?

options.A: Authority for clinical choices rests directly with the bedside nurse.
options.B: Nurse managers handle every single choice regarding patient hygiene.
options.C: All hospital decisions must be approved by the chief medical director.
options.D: Patients make all of their own medical treatment decisions alone.

explanation: Decentralized just means power is shared! The nurse right there at the bedside has the backing to make immediate, smart clinical choices for their patient. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T3#GNS123_U1_T3_h2)

question: In healthcare finance, what does 'opportunity cost' mean?

options.A: The value of the next best alternative given up when a choice is made
options.B: The total cost of operating a hospital for one calendar year
options.C: The penalty fee charged for mismanaged nursing budgets
options.D: The financial profit made from treating emergency patients

explanation: Opportunity cost is simply what you have to give up when you choose option A over option B. Every choice has a trade-off! [learn more](GST322_U2_T2#GST322_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which chemical messenger in the brain primarily acts to inhibit electrical activity and calm neurons down?

options.A: Sodium
options.B: Glutamate
options.C: GABA
options.D: Calcium

explanation: GABA is the main inhibitory neurotransmitter that helps prevent excessive electrical firing in the brain. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h2)

question: What is the main job of insulin at the cellular level?

options.A: It converts dietary protein directly into red blood cells
options.B: It signals the kidneys to absorb more sugar into the bloodstream
options.C: It destroys excess bacteria circulating in the plasma
options.D: It acts as a key to unlock cell receptors and let glucose inside

explanation: You can picture insulin as a tiny key. It unlocks the doors of our body cells so glucose from the food we eat can go inside and give us energy. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which antibiotic is commonly prescribed first-line for animal and human bite injuries?

options.A: Erythromycin ointment
options.B: Ciprofloxacin drops
options.C: Amoxicillin-clavulanate
options.D: Vancomycin syrup

explanation: Amoxicillin-clavulanate is a great choice because it covers the wide variety of bacteria typically found lurking in human and animal mouths. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T11#GNS221_U3_T11_h5)

question: Why must healthcare workers share disease outbreak data quickly with sanitation departments?

options.A: To help police officers arrest individuals who caused the epidemic
options.B: To ensure that international media houses report positive news updates
options.C: To determine the monthly salaries of environmental health inspectors
options.D: To allow sanitation teams to quickly target water safety interventions

explanation: Sharing health data lets sanitation teams quickly fix contaminated water sources and stop an infection from spreading further. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T8#GNS315_U5_T8_h5)

question: When are the three safety checks supposed to be done on a medication container?

options.A: When retrieving, preparing, and administering the drug
options.B: At the end of the shift during documentation handover
options.C: Whenever the patient complains of a new side effect
options.D: Only when ordering the medication from the hospital pharmacy

explanation: You got it! Checking the label three times—when you pick it up, when you prep it, and right before giving it—keeps your patient safe. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T3#GNS125_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of plotting a partograph during labor in a rural clinic?

options.A: To measure the exact birth weight of the newborn infant
options.B: To record the baby's future immunization appointments
options.C: To monitor the progress of labor and detect deviations early
options.D: To calculate the total financial cost of the hospital stay

explanation: The partograph is a visual tool used to track cervical dilation and fetal condition, helping midwives spot prolonged labor promptly. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h4)

question: A nurse wonders if a self-care theory works for elderly patients in rural farming communities. Where does this research idea come from?

options.A: Biomedical laboratory equipment maintenance
options.B: Professional theories and conceptual frameworks
options.C: Hospital financial accounting records
options.D: Direct pharmaceutical marketing campaigns

explanation: Testing established nursing models on new groups of people is a fantastic way to grow our professional knowledge. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T3#GNS217_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which type of facility usually provides secondary level healthcare services?

options.A: General hospitals
options.B: Teaching hospitals
options.C: Traditional herbal shops
options.D: Primary health centres

explanation: Well done! General hospitals step in when patients need doctors who specialize in specific areas, minor surgeries, or admission beyond what a primary health center can handle. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h2)

question: What is the main job of UNOCHA during an international crisis?

options.A: Directly manufacturing and distributing pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: Coordinating humanitarian relief efforts among multiple organizations
options.C: Training local nurses in bedside clinical procedures
options.D: Providing armed military defense for disaster zones

explanation: Spot on! UNOCHA acts like the ultimate coordinator, making sure all the different groups rushing to help are working together smoothly. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T10#GNS315_U1_T10_h2)

question: Why is collaboration with traditional and religious leaders important in community mental health care?

options.A: They replace the need for professional nurses and social workers entirely
options.B: They provide the financial funding for all federal hospital budgets
options.C: They hold significant influence and can help mobilize the community against stigma
options.D: They are legally required to write official psychiatric prescriptions

explanation: Because many community members trust local and religious leaders, their involvement helps change negative attitudes and encourages families to seek help early. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h4)

question: Which of the following is a primary nursing duty for a post-surgical home care patient?

options.A: Performing major surgical operations inside the home
options.B: Changing wound dressings and watching for signs of infection
options.C: Prescribing new antibiotics without a doctor's approval
options.D: Forcing the patient to run marathons to regain strength

explanation: Wound monitoring and dressing changes are core nursing responsibilities during acute recovery at home. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a community needs assessment?

options.A: To replace traditional healers with western doctors
options.B: To identify specific health burdens, preferences, and resource gaps
options.C: To determine which hospitals receive the most funding
options.D: To punish communities that ignore public health warnings

explanation: Spot on! Before starting any health program, a needs assessment helps nurses figure out what local challenges and resources look like on the ground. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T14#GNS313_U2_T14_h3)

question: Why must a nurse check their license jurisdiction before giving tele-nursing care?

options.A: It guarantees the nurse will receive a higher salary from the government.
options.B: Nurses must be legally authorized to practice in the physical location where the patient is situated.
options.C: Patients prefer nurses who live in foreign countries.
options.D: It ensures the tele-health software will run without internet connection issues.

explanation: Always remember: legally, you can only practice where you hold a valid license to protect your patients and your career. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h4)

question: In a typical clinic or hospital, about how much of the total waste generated is ordinary non-hazardous general rubbish?

options.A: 50 to 60 percent
options.B: 75 to 90 percent
options.C: 10 to 25 percent
options.D: 95 to 99 percent

explanation: You'd be surprised! The vast majority of waste coming from wards is just ordinary paper, food wrappings, and packaging—leaving only a small fraction that needs special hazardous care. [learn more](GST114_U6_T9#GST114_U6_T9_h1)

question: How does showing respect for a family's household customs help your patient care?

options.A: It allows the nurse to change household rules permanently
options.B: It reduces the financial cost of medical supplies
options.C: It builds trust and encourages the family to cooperate with the care plan
options.D: It guarantees the patient will never experience complications

explanation: Brilliant! When people feel respected in their own homes, they trust you more—and a trusting patient is much more likely to follow your health advice. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T10#GNS324_U1_T10_h5)

question: Why do cancer drugs (cytotoxic drugs) cause hair loss and upset stomachs?

options.A: The drugs accumulate exclusively in the skin
options.B: Healthy cells actively absorb the toxins
options.C: These healthy tissues also divide rapidly
options.D: The immune system attacks the medicine

explanation: Great thinking! Because these drugs target fast division, they accidentally affect normal body parts that also grow quickly, like hair roots and stomach lining. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T7#GNS215_U6_T7_h1)

question: What is the main idea behind Charting by Exception (CBE)?

options.A: Only physicians are allowed to write progress notes
options.B: Only abnormal or unusual findings are documented
options.C: Documentation is done exclusively at the end of the week
options.D: Every single nursing action must be written in detail

explanation: CBE is a huge time-saver! It assumes everything is normal unless you write down a specific exception or problem. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T6#GNS113_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the most common opportunistic infection and leading cause of death in people with HIV?

options.A: Tetanus
options.B: Tuberculosis
options.C: Cholera
options.D: Malaria

explanation: Tuberculosis (TB) is the top opportunistic infection we watch out for in patients with weakened immune systems. Catching it early saves lives! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h8)

question: Which vital sign should you keep an eye on when a patient is on long-term NSAID therapy?

options.A: Pupillary reflex
options.B: Oxygen saturation
options.C: Respiratory rate
options.D: Blood pressure

explanation: NSAIDs can cause the body to hold onto extra sodium and water, which often bumps up the blood pressure. Always a good vital sign to track! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T4#GNS223_U5_T4_h6)

question: Why is it essential to remove patient names from research data?

options.A: To reduce the number of pages in the final research report
options.B: To protect patient privacy and maintain strict confidentiality
options.C: To ensure all participants receive financial payment
options.D: To make computer software run much faster during analysis

explanation: Patient confidentiality is sacred in nursing. Anonymizing data ensures nobody's private medical details are accidentally exposed. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T16#GNS217_U3_T16_h7)

question: Generally, how many times should a specific joint movement be repeated during an AROM session?

options.A: One hundred times
options.B: Only once per shift
options.C: Two to five times
options.D: Until the patient faints

explanation: Keep it gentle! Repeating a motion just a few times helps the patient gain benefits without wearing them out. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which common habit in the ward is a leading cause of accidental needle-prick injuries for nursing staff?

options.A: Recapping used injection needles
options.B: Using needleless intravenous systems
options.C: Emptying full sharps containers safely
options.D: Placing sharps boxes at eye level

explanation: Never try to recap a used needle! Trying to guide that tiny cap back on with two hands is the number one way nurses accidentally jab their own fingers. [learn more](GST114_U6_T9#GST114_U6_T9_h4)

question: What does a grassroots approach to community health rely on most?

options.A: Complete reliance on imported foods for malnourished children
options.B: Strict enforcement of police patrols around local markets
options.C: Direct funding and management by foreign governments only
options.D: Active involvement and ownership by local community members

explanation: Grassroots programs succeed by empowering local residents to lead and sustain health initiatives within their own homes and villages. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T9#GNS225_U6_T9_h8)

question: How do nurses properly check for pitting oedema at the bedside?

options.A: Measuring the circumference of the limb with a flexible tape measure
options.B: Squeezing the muscle belly firmly to test for deep pain reflexes
options.C: Pressing a finger firmly against the swollen skin over a bony area for a few seconds
options.D: Applying a cold pack to see how fast the skin temperature drops

explanation: You got it! Pressing firmly over a bone (like the shin) pushes the fluid aside momentarily. If an indent stays behind, that's a positive 'pit'! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h4)

question: What does a dermatome represent in physical assessment?

options.A: A reflex arc located in the lower spine
options.B: The protective covering around the spinal cord
options.C: An area of skin supplied by a single spinal nerve
options.D: A group of muscles controlled by one motor nerve

explanation: A dermatome is a skin segment that receives its sensory innervation from one specific spinal nerve. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h8)

question: How does low health awareness usually affect when people go to the hospital?

options.A: It often delays people from seeking care until their sickness gets really bad
options.B: It makes them rush in immediately for minor surgeries
options.C: It forces patients to only use expensive private hospitals
options.D: It stops communities from needing health education entirely

explanation: Exactly. When people don't recognize early signs of illness, they often stay at home or use local herbs, only visiting the clinic when things turn into an emergency. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h2)

question: Who should ideally test out a draft questionnaire in the pre-testing phase?

options.A: Only senior professors who have published many research papers
options.B: Patients who have already completed the final main survey
options.C: Hospital accountants who manage the research funding budget
options.D: People who share similar characteristics with your target study group

explanation: Pre-testing works best when done with individuals who resemble your actual study participants so they can give realistic feedback. You're doing brilliantly! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h6)

question: How does placing an advanced breathing tube (like an endotracheal tube) change how CPR is performed?

options.A: Rescuers can give continuous compressions without pausing for breaths
options.B: Medications can only be given directly through the breathing tube
options.C: Chest compressions are stopped entirely while artificial breaths are given
options.D: Defibrillation pads are no longer needed once the tube is inserted

explanation: Once the tube is secured, teamwork gets easier—compressors can keep pushing without stopping to give breaths every few seconds! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T7#GNS315_U3_T7_h7)

question: Which of these is a great example of a well-written community health goal?

options.A: To teach nurses how to write better charts during night shifts
options.B: To reduce childhood malnutrition in Ward 4 by 20% within six months
options.C: To talk about malaria prevention whenever people visit the clinic
options.D: To make sure everybody in the whole country feels much healthier this year

explanation: Brilliant! This goal is specific, tells you where it's happening, gives a clear percentage, and sets a realistic timeframe. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h5)

question: What is the main reason farmers use crop rotation in their fields?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any water source
options.B: Restoring soil fertility and breaking pest cycles
options.C: Ensuring that only one crop grows forever in a field
options.D: Increasing the retail price of vegetables

explanation: Rotating different crops is a smart farming trick. It gives the soil a break to regain nutrients and confuses pests so they don't take over! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T024#GNS227_U2_T024_h2)

question: Which of these is a mistake to avoid when translating IEC materials for a local community?

options.A: Translating the message into the primary local language of the community
options.B: Using clear local symbols and pictorial representations
options.C: Using literal word-for-word translation without checking local meaning
options.D: Involving local community leaders to explain key terms

explanation: Word-for-word translations can completely twist the meaning of health instructions. Always check how locals actually say it! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T4#GNS124_U5_T4_h5)

question: At which stage of the family life cycle do parents adjust to the birth of their first infant?

options.A: Childbearing family stage
options.B: Launching center stage
options.C: Beginning family stage
options.D: Aging family stage

explanation: The childbearing stage starts right when that first baby arrives, bringing brand new joys and sleepless nights! [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is a crucial nursing duty BEFORE transferring a stabilized disaster victim to another hospital?

options.A: Remove all wound dressings for final inspection
options.B: Discontinue all intravenous fluids to save equipment
options.C: Wait for family members to sign financial clearance
options.D: Ensure secure lines, stable vitals, and handover notes

explanation: Spot on! Before they roll out, make sure their IV lines are secure, vitals are stable, and the receiving team has clear notes to continue good care. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T4#GNS315_U5_T4_h9)

question: What is a baby or toddler's most important emotional need?

options.A: Secure attachment and safety
options.B: Financial independence
options.C: Meaningful career advancement
options.D: Peer group validation

explanation: Little ones rely completely on their caregivers. Feeling safe and securely bonded is the bedrock of their future emotional health. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T5#GNS314_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the most common heart rhythm seen when a child goes into cardiac arrest?

options.A: Atrial fibrillation with rapid response
options.B: Pulseless ventricular tachycardia
options.C: Ventricular fibrillation
options.D: Asystole or pulseless electrical activity

explanation: Unlike adults who often arrest with a shockable rhythm like VF, children usually arrest after a long period of low oxygen, leading straight to asystole or PEA. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T3#GNS212_U2_T3_h7)

question: Which special part of the kidney detects a drop in blood pressure and releases renin?

options.A: Juxtaglomerular apparatus
options.B: Collecting duct
options.C: Bowman's capsule
options.D: Loop of Henle

explanation: Nice work! The juxtaglomerular apparatus acts like the kidney's security guard, sensing low pressure and releasing renin to kick off the body's blood-pressure-raising system. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T8#GNS121_U2_T8_h3)

question: In quantitative research, what does 'reliability' mean for a measurement tool?

options.A: Freedom from ethical violations
options.B: Generalizability to outside hospital populations
options.C: Accuracy in measuring the intended concept
options.D: Consistency of measurement scores over time

explanation: Reliability is all about consistency. If you use the tool again under the same conditions, you should get similar, steady results. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T4#GNS224_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an ethical practice when presenting qualitative research results?

options.A: Revealing the real names of participants to give them credit
options.B: Reporting all findings honestly, even unexpected ones
options.C: Separating factual results from personal opinions
options.D: Using pseudonyms to protect participant confidentiality

explanation: Participant confidentiality is paramount; revealing real names without explicit consent breaches ethical research standards. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why do doctors often prefer Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) over sharp metal instruments for early pregnancy care?

options.A: It permanently prevents future pregnancies without hormones
options.B: It eliminates the need for any pre-procedure counseling
options.C: It requires general anesthesia in a major operating theatre
options.D: It carries a lower risk of uterine perforation and trauma

explanation: Exactly! MVA uses gentle suction and soft tubes, which is much safer for the delicate walls of the uterus. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h4)

question: What is the main difference between hospital nursing and community nursing?

options.A: Hospital care focuses on acute cure, while community care focuses on prevention
options.B: Hospital care deals exclusively with healthy populations
options.C: Hospital care avoids technology, while community care uses advanced surgery
options.D: Community care only treats patients admitted to intensive care units

explanation: You nailed it. Hospitals treat sudden, severe illness, while community nursing is all about stopping sickness before it starts and keeping people well. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T7#GNS225_U1_T7_h3)

question: Which of these male reproductive parts is tucked safely inside the pelvic cavity?

options.A: Vas deferens
options.B: Scrotum
options.C: Testes
options.D: Penis

explanation: Think of the vas deferens as an internal highway located inside the pelvic cavity, while the scrotum and penis hang outside where we can see them. You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U4_T2#GNS121_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a basic facility needed for a healthy school environment?

options.A: Clean drinking water
options.B: An Olympic-sized swimming pool
options.C: Functional toilet facilities
options.D: A well-equipped sick bay

explanation: Correct! While a big pool is fun, basic health needs are all about clean water, good toilets, and a clinic space to care for sick students. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical challenge faced in Nigerian healthcare budgeting?

options.A: Inflation driving up the cost of imported medical drugs
options.B: Delays in the official release of approved budget allocations
options.C: Instantaneous release of excess government funds every single week
options.D: Unpredictable revenue caused by low health insurance coverage

explanation: Delayed funding releases are a known challenge, so instantaneous weekly funding is incorrect. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h7)

question: Which complication happens when high ventilator pressures cause tiny air sacs to rupture and air leaks into the chest cavity?

options.A: Pulmonary edema
options.B: Atelectasis
options.C: Pneumothorax
options.D: Pleural effusion

explanation: Too much pressure can pop overstretched alveoli, letting air leak into the space around the lung and causing it to collapse (a pneumothorax). [learn more](GNS315_U3_T6#GNS315_U3_T6_h6)

question: What is a common barrier to tele-nursing in rural areas?

options.A: Strict government laws banning telephone conversations
options.B: Digital illiteracy and lack of modern devices
options.C: An excess of high-end personal computers in every home
options.D: Patients refusing care because they live too close to clinics

explanation: Spot on. Many rural dwellers might not own smartphones or know how to navigate digital apps easily. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h7)

question: What severe medical condition is directly caused by prolonged, blocked labor in young girls whose pelvises are not yet fully grown?

options.A: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.B: Obstetric fistula
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Pregnancy-induced hypertension

explanation: Well done! The baby's head presses too long against an immature pelvis, creating a hole between the birth canal and bladder or rectum. This leads to constant leakage. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T11#GNS312_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is the main focus of quantitative research?

options.A: Historical observation of ancient medical texts
options.B: Open-ended interviews about emotional trauma
options.C: Numerical measurement and statistical analysis
options.D: Detailed personal stories of patient suffering

explanation: Quantitative research is all about numbers, counting, and statistics. If you can measure it, it's quantitative! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T6#GNS224_U1_T6_h2)

question: What defines a mass casualty incident (MCI)?

options.A: An emergency that only happens inside a surgical theatre
options.B: A routine medical ward shift with high patient turnover
options.C: Any situation where a single patient arrives in an ambulance
options.D: Patient numbers and injuries overwhelm available local resources

explanation: An MCI happens when the scale of the emergency outstrips the normal staff, space, and supplies of the hospital or clinic. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T1#GNS315_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why do HMOs place a strong emphasis on preventive health services?

options.A: To increase the out-of-pocket bills for the enrollees
options.B: To comply with international travel regulations
options.C: To force patients to visit doctors every single week
options.D: To catch illnesses early and lower expensive treatment costs

explanation: Preventing diseases or treating them early is much cheaper for the HMO than paying for complex, prolonged hospital admissions later. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why is a blame-free reporting culture so helpful for improving safety on hospital wards?

options.A: It speeds up the process of investigating patient complaints about pain
options.B: It allows the hospital to avoid paying for expensive safety-engineered needles
options.C: It encourages staff to report near-misses and hazards so systemic fixes can be made
options.D: It ensures that nurses never face disciplinary action for deliberate negligence

explanation: When staff feel safe speaking up without fear of being shouted at or punished, everyone can work together to fix dangerous workplace problems. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T4#GNS122_U4_T4_h7)

question: What kind of lubricant should you put on a nasogastric tube before sliding it in?

options.A: Sterile mineral oil
options.B: Antiseptic surgical gel
options.C: Water-soluble lubricant
options.D: Petroleum jelly ointment

explanation: We use a water-soluble jelly so that if a tiny bit accidentally goes into the lungs, the body absorbs it safely without causing pneumonia. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h3)

question: How does reading past literature help a nurse choose a new research topic?

options.A: It provides a list of patients who agreed to join the study

question: Which important vitamin is made by the friendly bacteria living in your large intestine?

question: Why is avoiding a fever important for a patient recovering from cardiac arrest?

question: Why do nurse researchers read past studies before starting a new project?

question: During drug breakdown, what actually happens in a chemical process called hydrolysis?

question: Which spinal nerve roots combine to form the brachial plexus?

question: Why do patients with upper motor neuron injuries often develop tight, spastic muscles over time?

question: Which setting is best for an older adult who needs round-the-clock nursing checks and complex wound care?

question: Who typically conducts follow-up visits or phone checks during a patient's trial leave?

question: If a patient mentions they first visited a traditional or spiritual healer before coming to the hospital, how should a nurse respond?

question: Which of these is NOT a common system challenge in many healthcare settings?

question: Which severe obstetric complication is frequently linked to early childbearing before the pelvis is fully developed?

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take after experiencing a needle-stick injury?

question: Why is it unsafe to plug multiple heavy medical devices into a single household power strip?

question: What happens right after a hormone hooks up with its target receptor?

question: Why is the pelvic floor shaped like a hammock?

question: Your patient looks really nervous before you check their tummy (abdomen). What should you do first?

question: How much energy does one gram of dietary fat provide compared to carbohydrates?

question: Why should you and your patient set nutrition goals together instead of you just giving orders?

question: How do people usually catch an Ascaris infection?

question: How does reading professional nursing journals help you find a great research topic?

question: How do indirect care technologies ultimately benefit patients?

question: Why are pregnant women told to avoid unpasteurized dairy and deli meats?

question: Why do babies of young mothers often face more malnutrition and infections as they grow?

options.B: Cultural laws forbid young mothers from feeding their babies solid foods
options.C: Infants born to young mothers have stronger immune systems that reject food
options.D: The young mother often lacks the knowledge, resources, and autonomy for proper childcare

question: How do pulmonary blood vessels react to an area of the lung that lacks proper ventilation?

options.A: They constrict to redirect blood to better ventilated areas
options.B: They burst open to release stored oxygen reserves into the tissue
options.C: They dilate to force more blood into the poorly ventilated alveoli
options.D: They completely shut down the entire right side of the heart

explanation: Pulmonary vessels automatically constrict in poorly ventilated areas, ensuring blood is sent to parts of the lung where oxygen is actually available. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h6)

options.B: Participative

options.D: Laissez-faire

question: Which sign is a nurse most likely to notice in a newborn with an open heart shunt like PDA?

question: What distinguishes a true behaviour disorder from normal teenage rebellion?

options.B: Persistent actions violating rights and norms
options.C: Temporary sadness after failing an exam
options.D: Occasional arguments with parents

question: What are the three core things a basic computer does?

question: Why is checking the publication date important when reading health articles online?

options.D: Medical guidelines and treatment practices change as new research emerges

question: What does hyperreflexia during a neurological exam usually point to?

options.A: Complete destruction of the sensory receptors in the skin
options.B: A lower motor neuron injury affecting peripheral nerves
options.C: An upper motor neuron lesion in the brain or spinal cord
options.D: Severe dehydration leading to temporary muscle cramps

explanation: Normally, the brain keeps our reflexes in check. When upper motor neurons are damaged, that control is lost, making reflexes overly jumpy (hyperreflexia). [learn more](GNS211_U3_T27#GNS211_U3_T27_h5)

question: What is an economic 'externality'?

options.A: An effect of a transaction that impacts third parties not directly involved
options.B: An unexpected side effect experienced after taking a new prescription pill
options.C: The tax paid by pharmaceutical companies on imported medical drugs
options.D: The total profit earned by a private hospital from foreign patients

explanation: An externality is a spillover effect. It happens when something you do affects other people around you who didn't take part in the original action. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h6)
